title: BEAD performance testing: operational networks must preserve technology, speed-tier, and subscriber-sample denominators
summary: NTIA requires annual testing during the period of performance and before closeout, with at least 100/20 Mbps for funded broadband locations, 1 Gbps symmetric for community anchor institutions, at least 95 percent of latency tests at or below 100 milliseconds, and average outages no greater than 48 hours over 365 days excluding force majeure. Denominator: Operational BEAD-funded service by eligible entity, technology, speed tier, and random active-subscriber sample; sample floors are five locations at 50 or fewer subscribers, 10 percent at 51-500, and 50 at 500 or more.
key_findings: Finding: NTIA requires annual testing during the period of performance and before closeout, with at least 100/20 Mbps for funded broadband locations, 1 Gbps symmetric for community anchor institutions, at least 95 percent of latency tests at or below 100 milliseconds, and average outages no greater than 48 hours over 365 days excluding force majeure.

Denominator: Operational BEAD-funded service by eligible entity, technology, speed tier, and random active-subscriber sample; sample floors are five locations at 50 or fewer subscribers, 10 percent at 51-500, and 50 at 500 or more.
Boundary: These are required measures, not observed results.
Boundary: Testing applies to operational service and is not construction validation.
Boundary: A passing sample does not establish universal adoption, affordability, or economic outcomes.
Next action: Publish eligible-entity results only when the tested cohort, technology, speed tier, sample, period, exclusions, and closeout status are disclosed.
